title: One More Motivation to Use Evaluation Tools This Time for Hardware Multiplicative Masking of AES
problem: Prior hardware implementations of multiplicative masking for AES contain critical vulnerabilities in the Kronecker delta function that leak information under side-channel analysis.
motivation: AES is the most widely used encryption standard; defending against side-channel attacks requires rigorous evaluation of masking implementations using formal tools.
method: The researchers evaluate a prior multiplicative masking design (from De Meyer et al. 2018) using the PROLEAD evaluation tool. This tool searches for side-channel leakage—ways that sensitive information might escape through observable side effects like power consumption or timing—by testing the design under conditions that allow attackers to observe these effects. They find that the Kronecker delta function (which compares values and outputs 1 when they match, 0 otherwise) leaks information this way, particularly at the first-order level (the most direct form of leakage). They then propose a solution by optimizing the randomness used in the masking scheme.
key_novelty: The Kronecker delta function (a mathematical building block that detects when values match) in multiplicative masking designs has a leakage vulnerability that can be fixed through improved randomness optimization.
contributions: Discovered leakage in prior Kronecker delta implementation under formal evaluation
Proposed alternative randomness optimization addressing the vulnerability
Demonstrated effectiveness of fix using PROLEAD evaluation tool
baselines: De Meyer et al. (CHES 2018) multiplicative masking design
primary_theme: Side-channel secure multiplicative masking for AES
